public_rationale: Intercom's account describes useful production delegation, which challenges an absolute dismissal of autonomous work. It does not provide verified success and intervention rates sufficient to establish the required counterexample. Customer concerns about assumed resolutions further limit what headline rates can prove. Neither these limitations nor the continuing presence of human staff establishes that LLMs cannot reliably run any bounded workflow.
limitations: The operational account is a vendor disclosure.
The resolution-metric concern is customer testimony rather than an independent audit.
Different readings of trust and autonomy could change the result.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs cannot be trusted to run anything on their own.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are sold as “AI,” a technology best-known for automating things, yet they can’t be trusted to run anything on their own.

from_speaker: to run anything on their own
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a universal claim about practical autonomous operation, not a requirement that software never make an error.
A counterexample must reliably execute a defined workflow without case-by-case human approval or correction. Ordinary setup, maintenance and monitoring are allowed.
Marketing a workflow as automated or recording unanswered conversations as resolved does not itself establish reliability.
For this ongoing capability observation, use May 2026, the latest complete month before the post. No reporting cadence is specified, so this period choice is an evaluator interpretation.
criteria.support_condition: Broad operational evidence establishes that no relevant class of defined LLM workflow meets a reasonable task-specific reliability standard without case-by-case human supervision.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one production workflow in the target period demonstrably operates without case-by-case human supervision and meets a documented, task-appropriate standard for successful completion and errors.

evidence.excerpt: Fin had freed up significant capacity
evidence.explanation: Intercom describes an operating support arrangement with useful AI delegation and substantial continuing human work. The account supplies neither a verified autonomous success rate nor enough detail to establish that every delegated task requires supervision.
The customer describes why reported resolution rates may overstate verified success. This is a measurement caution, not proof that Fin fails or that autonomous LLM operation is impossible.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated May 2026 operational evaluation showing verified outcomes, errors and human interventions for a defined autonomous workflow, assessed against an explicit task-appropriate reliability standard.
